comment: The mutants of owner.place and owner.prover (src/fort/owner/) that make the pass prove a store
that it must not prove, against the oracle test of rule (a) (test/fort/owner/oracle_test.ft,
spec/ownership-design.md 3.6). Each row is a row of tools/mutations/emptiness.json with the same
anchor. A row is caught when the test fails: a false accept makes it exit 134, and a changed
count changes its stdout. The log of a round shows which. D17.11-memory-pointer changes only a
count, because the pass stays sound with it: a place through a pointer local that is memory
changes only by a store into the local, which kills each fact with its base, by a store through
a pointer or a call, which kill each fact reached through memory, or by a store into its
pointee, which kills as any store does. Of the 86 rows of tools/mutations/emptiness.json, 37 are
not here: 19 make the pass prove less, such as D17.11-memory-fixed, D17.11-straight-others,
D17.11-store-test-kills, D17.11-entry-temp and D17.11-scratch-entry; 6 change the work limit or
the verdicts past it, which no function of the sets reaches; 9 change the report, the driver or
the build-mode pass; and 3 prove more and change no verdict of a run. D17.11-below and
D17.11-key-return change no run: after the gen, an element of the span fails its bounds check
first, and only a store writes _0, which kills each fact with its key. D17.11-guard-edges proves
a check whose store the pass does not prove, and the site of that store stays rejected.
D17.11-held-fixed and D17.11-store-hidden-checked change only a count, because the pass stays
sound with them: the place of a held address of fixed storage reads as a local that is memory,
and the check that guards a store into an aggregate _0 with no proof stays unproved.
D17.11-entry-local changes only a count too: it gives a named local a fact at the entry, which
no case of the sets runs over a live allocation, and the first store of late_zero loses its
false reject. The table runs in the Linux VM with the debug preset and the default runner. The
md5 guard reads the product compiler, whose driver imports owner.prover. The first rounds of a
run can read stale (notes/testing.md 7), so the first row is one that a full run caught.
The rows D17.20 are the rows of tools/mutations/leak.json with the same anchor that make the
pass prove an exit of part 1 of the leak rule (D17.20) that a run leaks at; the test prints a
false accept of rule (c) part 1 for each. The rows D17.20-inner are the rows of
tools/mutations/leak.json with the same anchor for part 2 of the leak rule. D17.20-inner-del,
-cast, -walk, -fact, -owners, -element and -local make the pass prove a site of part 2 that a
run leaks at. The test prints a false accept of part 2 for each. D17.20-inner-local needs the
case `inner` of the gate, which frees an object through a field of a base pointer. The first
owner of the object of that pointer is empty, and the mutant reads that owner in place of the
owner of the object. D17.20-inner-memory changes only a count: no run of the sets breaks a
proof that it adds (the logs of the rounds). A store through a pointer and a call kill each
fact through a memory pointer local, as for D17.11-memory-pointer.
D17.11-held-memory needs the FIR case held_reach. A copy through the address of the held
address is a second pointer to its place. The mutant keeps the fact of the fresh base pointer
over a store through that copy. The test then prints a false accept at the next store.
The rows D17.20-check-exit and D17.20-abort hold the abort blocks of part 1 of the leak rule
(D17.20). D17.20-check-exit drops the obligation of a `dead` in a block that ends in a
`check`. The case `before_check` of the gate then fails the gate, and the test prints a false
accept. The rows D17.20-abort change fir.term_is_abort (src/fort/fir.ft). The pass and the
judge of the test both read that function, so the judge follows the pass. A case holds each
part of it. `before_check` holds a `check`, and `abort_block` holds a `fail`. The FIR case
leak_abort holds a `trap`, and the case `unreachable` of the gate holds an `unreachable`. A
row of FORCED stops the test for D17.20-abort-check, -fail, -none and -all. D17.20-abort-trap
and D17.20-abort-unreachable make the pass refuse an item that it accepts. The test then
stops below the row of the hand family in FLOORS.
The rows D17.20-owning change types.type_is_owning_aggregate, and the rows D17.1-reference
change types.type_is_reference (src/fort/types.ft). The pass and the judge both read these
functions too. Such a mutant is also in the compiler that builds the test, so a row can go
red before a case runs. To measure the cases alone, compile the test with a compiler with no
mutant, from a tree with the mutant in src/. The rest of this paragraph is that measurement.
The limit: a run of this table stops for 8 rows when the compiler with the mutant builds
std. The 8 rows are D17.20-owning-none and D17.20-owning-struct, the 5 rows D17.1-reference,
and D17.11-reads-none (src/fort/fir.ft). For these rows the run holds that the compiler with
the mutant does not build std. It does not hold the case of the row.
The case struct_move of the uses does not check for D17.20-owning-none and
D17.20-owning-struct. The hand case fa1 fails the gate for D17.20-owning-array and
D17.20-owning-direct, and the case `nested_array` of the gate for D17.20-owning-nested. The
sandbox runtime (test/fort/support/run_env.ft) does not check for D17.1-reference-none, -void
and -span, and the hand case fa1 for D17.1-reference-pointer. The case `string_owner` of the
gate does not check for D17.1-reference-string.
The rows D17.11-reads change fir.stmt_reads (src/fort/fir.ft), which gives each operand of a
statement. The pass reads it, and so does take_named of the judge. With D17.11-reads-none the
compiler refuses a declaration of the first batch. That is the measurement with a compiler
with no mutant. In a run of this table the row stops before that, at std (the limit above).
With D17.11-reads-callee the item of the
FIR case const_call takes no error of leak_temp, and fails the gate. D17.11-reads-del changes
only the stdout: the `del` of the FIR case del_join keeps its pointer fresh, and two false
rejects of that case go. Only the pass holds that row, because take_named reads a constant of
a function and a `del` reads a `move`.
The rows D17.11-test are the rows of tools/mutations/emptiness.json with the same anchor that
make a test against null prove too much: no kill after its read, the edge of the other value, a
`not` that keeps the value, a store into a tested scratch local that keeps its bit, and an edge
set on each edge. The test prints a false accept for each.
The rows D17.11-alias are the rows of tools/mutations/emptiness.json with the same anchor that
make refinement R6 (src/fort/owner/alias.ft) keep a fact that a store through a pointer can
kill; the hand cases k2, n4a and k2r to k2l print a false accept for each.
The rows D17.21 are the rows of tools/mutations/vacated.json with the same anchor that make the
pass prove a use of rule (b) of D17.21 that a run reads after a `move` or a `del`; the test
prints a false accept of rule (b) for each and exits 134. D17.21-test-both needs the hand case
null_edge, whose load stands on the edge where its test finds null, and D17.21-global
needs the hand case global_ptr, whose load goes through a global. D17.21-error, the row of
tools/mutations/vacated.json with the same anchor, makes an unproved use no error: the test
rejects a use of rule (b) only with the error (has_error), so it prints a false accept for it.
The rows D17.20-aggregate make the pass prove an exit of a local of an owning aggregate type
that a run leaks at, an exit that part 1 of the leak rule makes an error: the test prints a
false accept of the owning aggregate locals for each and exits 134. D17.20-aggregate-error, the
row of tools/mutations/aggregate.json with the same anchor, makes such an unproved exit no
error: the test rejects such an exit only with the error (has_error), so it prints a false
accept for it.
